question: Can linear Fisher information about a continuous physical parameter be tracked through hidden layers and used to stop neural-network training without a held-out validation set?

key_findings.claim: The method estimates parameter-relevant information at each layer using a linear Fisher-information lower bound computed from sample means and covariances.
key_findings.evidence: Finite differences across nearby parameter values estimate the derivative of the layerwise mean, and its covariance-weighted quadratic form yields linear Fisher information. By the data-processing inequality, deterministic layers cannot create true Fisher information; the linear estimator is conservative and becomes exact only when a linear unbiased estimator is sufficient.

anchors.section: II.B-D Fisher information and linear Fisher information

key_findings.claim: The reported hidden-layer profiles show networks learning to preserve parameter information while compressing images to a scalar estimate.
key_findings.evidence: Across training checkpoints, early models lose information through depth, near-optimal models transmit nearly the input information to the output, and overtrained models again lose output information. This is demonstrated on simulated images and an optical object-position experiment.

key_findings.claim: The proposed early-stopping rule infers expected estimator error from training loss and stops when output Fisher information is maximal, avoiding a validation split in the tested estimation setting.
key_findings.evidence: The rule connects mean-squared error, bias, and the Cramer-Rao lower bound, then selects the epoch at which information transmission peaks. The paper reports close alignment with minimum test error on synthetic and experimental data, but applicability presumes a near-efficient estimator and an adequate estimate of input information.

anchors.section: IV Early Stopping Based on Fisher Information

key_findings.claim: The approach is local in parameter value and can become inaccurate with small data, broad parameter ranges, biased estimators, or poorly conditioned covariances.
key_findings.evidence: The discussion states that a global criterion needs evaluations at multiple parameter values unless Fisher information is nearly constant, and notes finite-difference, covariance, and dataset-size limits. The experimental mismatch from the ideal bound is linked partly to the finite training range.

method.core_idea: Use a moment-based lower bound on Fisher information as a layerwise conservation diagnostic for continuous-parameter estimators.
method.mechanism: Collect samples at nearby parameter settings, propagate them through every layer, estimate mean derivatives and covariances, compute linear Fisher information, and select the training checkpoint where output information—and predicted attainable precision—peaks.
assumptions: The physical parameter is continuous and nearby parameter-conditioned samples are available.
Layer covariance matrices can be estimated and regularized reliably.
Linear Fisher information is a close proxy for full Fisher information in the relevant representation.
The learned estimator is sufficiently close to the Cramer-Rao regime for the stopping relation.
Parameter dependence is locally smooth at the finite-difference scale.

techniques.role: Provides a conservative moment-based information estimate.
Tracks parameter-relevant information through internal representations.
Chooses a checkpoint without allocating a validation split.
Approximates derivatives with respect to the unknown physical parameter.

evaluations.metric: Layerwise normalized Fisher information and error versus epoch
evaluations.result: Peak output information is reported near minimum estimation error and falls with overtraining

evaluations.setting: Optical imaging experiment estimating object position
evaluations.result: The criterion approximately locates the best epoch despite a gap from the ideal Cramer-Rao bound
evaluations.baseline: Held-out performance and the input-information limit

evaluations.result: Profiles are sensitive to sample size, covariance estimation, and parameter range

limitations: Author-stated: the estimator is local in the unknown parameter and may need repeated evaluation across a range.
Author-stated: sufficient data are needed for stable covariance and finite-difference estimates.
Author-stated: the linear bound can be pessimistic when sufficient statistics are nonlinear.
Reviewer-identified: demonstrations concern scalar physical-parameter regression, not classification or open-ended prediction.
Reviewer-identified: using all training data at several controlled parameter values may be harder than reserving validation data in many applications.
failure_modes: A singular high-dimensional covariance makes the inverse unstable.
Finite-difference steps are too small for sampling noise or too large for locality.
Bias or non-identifiability prevents the Cramer-Rao relation from predicting error.
True information is stored nonlinearly while linear Fisher information falls.
Distribution shift changes input Fisher information after checkpoint selection.
reusable_insights: Track task-relevant rather than total information when representations are deterministic and mutual information is ill posed.
Treat information conservation as a diagnostic, not proof that a representation is sufficient.
Report sensitivity to finite-difference scale and covariance regularization.
Compare any validation-free stopping rule against matched held-out and repeated-seed baselines.
open_questions: Can nonlinear or neural Fisher estimators improve fidelity without prohibitive sample cost?
How should uncertainty in the Fisher estimate propagate into the stopping decision?
Does the rule remain reliable for vector parameters and nuisance variables?
Can it detect distribution shift rather than only within-distribution overfitting?
When is validation-free stopping actually more sample-efficient after accounting for parameter sweeps?

competitive_landscape.title: Deep Learning and the Information Bottleneck Principle
competitive_landscape.difference: Information-bottleneck work studies mutual information with input and target. This paper instead tracks Fisher information about a continuous physical parameter, avoiding deterministic-continuous mutual-information pathologies and deriving a task-specific stopping signal.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Information Bottleneck Theory of Deep Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Saxe et al. show that claimed mutual-information compression depends on nonlinearity and measurement choices. The present linear-Fisher diagnostic is more narrowly tied to estimation precision but inherits estimator-choice and finite-sample dependence.

competitive_landscape.title: How Does Information Bottleneck Help Deep Learning?
competitive_landscape.difference: Kawaguchi et al. relate information bottlenecks to generalization errors across learning settings. This paper offers a lower-cost physical-estimation diagnostic based on Fisher information and an early-stopping use case rather than a general learning bound.

competitive_landscape.title: Phase Transitions for the Information Bottleneck in Representation Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Wu and Fischer connect Fisher geometry to phase transitions of an information-bottleneck objective for categorical representation learning. The current work directly estimates data-parameter Fisher information through a trained regressor and uses its peak operationally.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: This is the first architecture-agnostic method to monitor Fisher information about a measured parameter through neural-network layers and turn maximal transmission into validation-free early stopping.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper derives a linear-Fisher estimator, visualizes its layerwise evolution, and tests stopping on synthetic and experimental imaging regressions.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Layerwise information analyses and Fisher-based representation theory are established. The novel, defensible increment is applying a conservative data-parameter Fisher estimate end-to-end as a practical stopping diagnostic for physical parameter estimation. General validation-free claims require broader tasks and calibrated uncertainty.

reviewer_notes: Read all 17 pages, including derivation, synthetic and optical experiments, discussion, statistical appendices, and references. Primary arXiv records for four information-theoretic comparators were checked on 2026-08-23. Exact plotted peak values were not digitized; claims are limited to values stated in text and qualitative figure relationships.
